title: The Gilded Veil Again
premise: The Gilded Veil is the last guild that trades in impossible things—bottled grief, borrowed years, names not yet spoken—and Lena Marchetti keeps its ledgers while the guild quietly dies around her. When a child arrives speaking a language older than kingdoms, Lena learns the boy is a fragment of the thing wearing King Aldric's crown: a parasite of borrowed power that has been unbinding itself from its host and scattering into vessels. Hunted by the Crown's inquisitors and betrayed by her own guildmaster, who sold the guild's charter to buy his own survival, Lena must gather the scattered fragments before they reassemble—and choose between destroying them and freeing the hollowed king. In the end she binds the parasite into the guild's oldest ledger, sacrificing the Veil's secrecy to do it, and the guild dies so that justice can finally live outside the law.
about_author: I. M. Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing merchant guild records in coastal trading cities. Their fiction blends bureaucratic precision with folklore, exploring what institutions owe the people they outlive.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unwritten Things
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The Gilded Veil's counting house is nearly empty; three members remain, and Master Corvane burns correspondence to hide how bad the debts are. Lena balances ledgers of impossible inventory alone at night, invisible by design. When a barefoot child appears at the sealed door speaking a language no living tongue knows, the wards answer him. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by wonder.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The boy, Tam, speaks only in fragments that make objects obey—candles relight, rust unwinds. Guildmate Oskar recognizes the cadence from forbidden texts: it predates the monarchy itself. Corvane orders the boy locked away until he 'can be appraised.' Lena secretly copies Tam's words into her ledger. Emotional beat: first act of quiet defiance.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Tam, rendered through Lena's translations. Tam dreams in another man's memories: King Aldric, drowning in his own coronation, something ancient sliding beneath his skin. The fragments are waking across the city—a singing well, a mad priestess, a coin that bleeds. Emotional beat: horror and pity entwined; Tam doesn't know if he is a boy or a piece of a monster.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: POV Lena. A royal inquisitor, Dame Serah Voss, arrives to inspect dying guilds' registries. Corvane offers to sell Tam's existence off the books. Lena falsifies the ledgers for the first time in her life, feeling the guild's old magic accept the lie. Emotional beat: terror transmuting into purpose—she has chosen a side.

chapters.title: Debts Written in Bone
chapters.summary: POV Oskar. The guild's history surfaces: generations ago, the Veil brokered the bargain that put the parasite on Aldric's line in exchange for its charter. The guild didn't trade in impossible things—it created one. Oskar, loyal to Corvane, discovers Lena's forged entries but says nothing. Emotional beat: complicity and guilt; belonging built on buried sin.

chapters.title: The Hollow King's Procession
chapters.summary: POV Lena. King Aldric rides publicly for the first time in years, smiling wrong, and every fragment in the city turns toward him like iron to lodestone. Tam begins to fade as the pieces call each other home. Voss catches Lena mid-escape with the boy and, instead of arresting her, reveals she serves the crown, not the king—and wants the parasite destroyed. Uneasy alliance forms. Emotional beat: fear giving way to fragile trust.

chapters.title: Charter of Ashes
chapters.summary: POV Corvane. Cornered by Voss's investigation, Corvane trades the guild's founding charter—the physical anchor of the original bargain—to the parasite's agents in exchange for his life. The Veil's protections collapse; inquisitors storm the counting house. Oskar dies holding the door, finally choosing the guild over his master. Emotional beat: betrayal crowned by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Reassembly
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Lena and Voss race to the coronation crypt where the fragments converge on Aldric. Tam, nearly dissolved, begs Lena to let him go home to the thing wearing the king. She refuses—not to save herself, but because she has learned the boy is also the only part of the parasite that ever wanted to belong. Climax begins: binding ritual improvised from ledger-craft, ink and debt and name. Emotional beat: love weaponized against power.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Unbound
chapters.summary: POV Lena, climax. In the crypt, Lena writes the parasite into the guild's oldest ledger—an accounting it cannot escape, since it was born of a contract. It fights with Aldric's stolen decades, offering her the guild restored, Corvane's crimes erased, everything she was denied. She enters the final figure anyway. The parasite is bound; Aldric collapses, hollow but alive; Tam remains, fully a boy. Emotional beat: costly victory, grief and release.

chapters.title: The Open Door
chapters.summary: POV Tam, closing with Lena. The Gilded Veil is officially dead, its secrets spilled; Voss rebuilds justice without charters or veils, and Corvane faces a human court rather than a magical one. Lena opens the counting house doors as a school for children who speak strange truths, Tam first among them. Belonging, she writes in the last clean ledger, cannot be appraised. Emotional beat: quiet hope after ruin.
